person_made_it: The Francksens are the cast: five faceless storybook portraits in the brief's colors (James burgundy, Henry red and green, Oscar orange and blue), and every joy card is a real moment from Eric's year.
emcee_who_is_speaking: A Gorey-style storybook narrator, turned kind: one italic line reacts to each play; Gordon appears only in his own quoted line.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: A sunny afternoon in front of an 1898 Queen Anne house, ending at a confetti sunrise.
did_the_click_pay_me: Cards slide and snap with a crisp card sound, gold seals sparkle, hearts fill, the family meter climbs, and at full joy every played card fans out into a crown before the Happily Ever After card and its music.
works_for_the_recipient: Phone: tap a card then a portrait (drag also works), 3-card hand, 3 plus 2 portrait grid. PC: 5 portraits in a row, 4-card hand, drag and drop with live +joy preview on hover, keys A S D F and 1 to 5. No fail state; Deal again restarts. Played to the ending in WebKit 390, Chromium 1920 and 2560.
taught_me_something: It explains Gloom's real mechanic, stacked clear cards where only the visible symbols count, and credits Sky Ship Studios with Atlas Games and Asmodee.
told_me_the_truth: Every card fact comes from the brief's fact list; no Gloom art or logo is used; the boys get colors only, no invented traits.
weakest: The strategy is shallow: with the joy target at 6 of 9 and an endless deck the game finishes in about 10 plays almost however you play, so the covering mechanic is felt more than it is mastered.
